name: Breadboard (830 points)
desc: A board full of holes for building circuits without soldering. Parts and wires just push in.

name: Jumper Wires (M-M, M-F, F-F)
desc: Pre-made wires with pins or sockets on the ends. Male-to-male for the breadboard, female ends for module pins.

name: Resistor Kit (220Ω–10kΩ)
desc: An assortment of common resistors: 100Ω, 220Ω, 330Ω, 1kΩ, 2kΩ, 4.7kΩ and 10kΩ. They limit current for LEDs and make pull-ups and voltage dividers.
note: Read values with the color bands or, easier, a multimeter.

name: USB Data Cable (for your board)
desc: Connects your board to the PC for uploading code and power. Match the plug: USB-B (Uno/Mega), Mini-B or USB-C (Nano), Micro-B or USB-C (ESP32/Pico).
note: Classic trap: some cables are charge-only and carry no data. If the PC doesn't see your board, try another cable first.

name: Ceramic Capacitors 100nF (0.1µF)
desc: Tiny capacitors (marked "104") that smooth out electrical noise. Used for decoupling and to stop buttons from "bouncing".

name: Electrolytic Capacitor Kit (1µF–1000µF)
desc: Can-shaped capacitors that store a bit of energy and steady the power supply. LED strips and radios love them.
note: Polarity matters: the stripe marks the − leg. Backwards or over-voltage, they can pop.

name: 1N4007 Diodes
desc: One-way valves for electricity. Placed backwards across a motor or relay coil, it soaks up the voltage spike when it switches off (a "flyback diode").
note: The silver stripe is the cathode (−) end. For a flyback diode, the stripe faces the + supply.

name: NPN Transistors (PN2222A / 2N2222)
desc: A small electronic switch: a weak pin current turns on a bigger current (up to ~500mA). Use it for buzzers, small motors and relays.
note: The pin order DIFFERS between makers: PN2222A is often E-B-C and P2N2222A is C-B-E. Check the datasheet for the exact marking on yours.

name: IRLZ44N Logic-Level MOSFET
desc: A heavy-duty electronic switch that lets a 5V pin control big loads like LED strips, pumps and motors (several amps).
voltage: Up to 55V · fully on with a 5V gate
note: Pins: Gate, Drain, Source (left to right, facing the label). Add a 10kΩ resistor from gate to GND.

warn.3.3: From a 3.3V pin the IRLZ44N only partly turns on: fine for loads under ~1A, but it can get hot with big motors.

name: Logic Level Shifter (4-ch, BSS138)
desc: A tiny translator between 3.3V and 5V signals, so a 3.3V board (ESP32/Pico) can safely talk to 5V modules.
note: Connect LV to 3.3V, HV to 5V, and both GNDs. Not fast enough for WS2812B strips (use a 74AHCT125 for those).

name: 1N5819 Schottky Diodes
desc: Fast diodes with a low voltage drop: better flyback diodes for PWM-driven motors, and reverse-polarity protection.

name: 1N4148 Signal Diodes
desc: Small, fast diodes for signals and logic tricks (not for motors).

name: BC547 NPN Transistors
desc: Small switching transistors for loads up to ~100mA, like buzzers and small LEDs.
note: Usual pin order (flat face toward you): C-B-E. Check the datasheet for your marking.

name: TIP120 Darlington Transistor
desc: A strong transistor (up to 5A) for motors and strips. It loses ~1.5–2V, so it runs warmer than a MOSFET.
note: Pins (label facing you): B-C-E. Still add a 1N4007 flyback diode across motors.

name: PC817 Optocoupler
desc: Passes a signal using light inside the chip, keeping two circuits electrically separate.
note: Its LED side needs a series resistor (about 1kΩ).

name: NE555 Timer IC
desc: The legendary timer chip: blinkers, tone generators and delays without any code.

name: 74HC595 Shift Register
desc: Turns 3 board pins into 8 outputs. Chain several to light dozens of LEDs.
note: Each LED still needs its own resistor; keep the total current under ~70mA.

name: CD4051 Analog Multiplexer (8:1)
desc: Lets one analog pin read 8 different sensors or knobs, one at a time.

name: LM358 Dual Op-Amp
desc: Amplifies small signals, such as a microphone or sensor, before your board reads them.

name: 74AHCT125 Level Shifter (for LED strips)
desc: A fast one-way 3.3V → 5V translator: the proper way to drive WS2812B LEDs from an ESP32 or Pico.
note: Tie the OE (enable) pins of used channels to GND.

name: TXS0108E 8-Channel Level Shifter
desc: Translates 8 signals between 3.3V and 5V automatically in both directions.
note: Not great for I2C with strong pull-ups: use the BSS138 type for I2C.

name: Ceramic Capacitor Kit (10pF–100nF)
desc: An assortment of small capacitors for filters, crystals and noise fixes.

name: Male Pin Headers (40-pin strips)
desc: Break-apart pin strips you solder onto modules so they plug into breadboards.

name: Female Pin Headers (40-pin strips)
desc: Sockets for plugging modules into your own boards, so they can be swapped later.

name: Perfboard / Protoboard (various sizes)
desc: A board with a grid of holes to solder a permanent version of your breadboard circuit.

name: Heat Shrink Tubing Kit
desc: Plastic sleeves that shrink with heat to insulate soldered wire joints neatly.
note: Shrink with a heat gun or carefully with the side of a soldering iron (not a lighter flame).

name: Screw Terminal Blocks (PCB, 2/3-pin)
desc: Clamp wires with a screwdriver: great for power and motor connections on perfboards.

name: Mini Breadboard (170 points)
desc: A tiny breadboard that sticks onto robots and boxes.

name: Half Breadboard (400 points)
desc: A medium breadboard: enough room for most single-sensor projects.

name: Pre-Cut Breadboard Wire Kit
desc: Flat, color-coded wires of exact lengths, for neat breadboard builds that are easy to debug.
